system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | What the buyer should want | Recommendation and reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A cap proportionate to the risk and diligence findings, with higher or uncapped recovery for specified serious claims and a separate, higher cap for tax/IP if appropriate. | **Reject as a blanket cap; negotiate a higher general cap and distinct carve-outs/caps.** A 20% cap may be inadequate against material undisclosed liabilities. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 tipping basket, with only the excess recoverable. | A lower de minimis and a tipping basket (recovery from dollar one once crossed), or a deductible basket only if reflected in price. | **Counter on both thresholds and seek tipping recovery from dollar one.** The proposed deductible basket leaves the buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000 of otherwise valid claims. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Notify general Warranty Claims within 18 months; seller seeks to apply any limitation to all Claims unless stated otherwise. | A longer period for general warranties, with distinct periods for tax, title/fundamental, fraud and claims that cannot reasonably be identified earlier. | **Reject the blanket application; specify separate, longer periods by claim type.** Tax and latent claims may emerge after 18 months, and notice periods should not unintentionally cut off other claims. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general cap and time limits. | Title, authority and capacity claims outside the general cap, with a separate high or full-price cap and an appropriately long period. | **Reject; negotiate a separate fundamental regime.** Defects in ownership or ability to transfer the shares go to the core of the transaction. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is stated. | Expressly exclude fraud and fraudulent concealment (and, as appropriate, deliberate breach) from caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. | **Add an express fraud carve-out.** The seller should not obtain contractual protection for its own fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire indexed data room, accounts, registers and public records, alongside specific disclosures. | Fair, specific disclosure against each warranty, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no blanket data-room or public-record disclosure. | **Reject general disclosure and require warranty-linked particulars.** The broad formulation risks deeming matters disclosed even where the buyer could not readily identify their relevance or extent. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records. | No broad constructive-knowledge bar; at most, a narrow exception for actual knowledge of designated senior deal personnel, with no waiver of claims for fraud or deliberate concealment. | **Reject the proposed qualifier.** “Discoverable” knowledge is uncertain and could turn diligence access into a waiver of negotiated protection. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. DD-002 shows ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%) and no final consent or evidence conditions are met. | A condition precedent requiring final, unconditional written consent and satisfaction/waiver of all associated conditions before completion; termination or other protection if not obtained. | **Make valid consent and conditions a completion condition, not merely delivery of a letter.** Bluefen is a material revenue concentration and the disclosed consent process remains incomplete. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | ~AUD 3.2m facility to be released after Completion; DD-003 says it remains outstanding with no final discharge. | Repayment at or before completion from seller proceeds, with lender payout evidence, release of security and evidence of discharge as completion deliverables; no residual company debt or security. | **Require payoff and release at completion.** A post-completion promise leaves the buyer exposed to debt and encumbrances after acquiring the company. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses are not separately itemised in the draft funds flow; payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unspecified. | Full identification and funding of bonus amounts and associated on-costs in the completion accounts/funds flow, borne by seller or treated as debt-like leakage, with no double counting. | **Resolve and fund the bonuses and on-costs before signing off on funds flow.** The disclosed amounts are omitted and the total exposure may exceed AUD 420,000. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; DD-004/010 indicate AUD 180,000 open, without independent proof of non-payment or assignment. | A specific indemnity covering all loss from failure to obtain valid ownership/assignment of the SOW3 Project Materials, including further fees, claims and remediation, with payment/assignment evidence as a completion condition where feasible. | **Expand the indemnity and require confirmation of payment and assignment.** The contract ties transfer to cleared payment, while the disclosure includes neither a receipt nor confirmatory assignment. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; no specific protection is proposed. DD-006 records an unintended external email link and possible 1,240 records, with access, scope and notification status unresolved. | A specific indemnity or tailored warranty for the incident, continued investigation and remediation covenants, timely updates, and appropriate notification/response controls; preserve claims irrespective of whether a breach is ultimately confirmed. | **Do not accept a materiality dismissal; require incident-specific protections and completion of a documented investigation.** The facts leave access, scope and notification obligations unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totaling AUD 330,000 characterised as ordinary-course operating costs; DD-008/011 do not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. | Full contract and liability details, confirmation of execution/termination terms and accrued amounts, and adjustment or specific protection for non-ordinary, undisclosed or avoidable commitments. | **Require particulars and assess them in completion adjustments and warranties.** The disclosure does not establish that these costs are ordinary-course or unavoidable. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; seller also seeks to apply time limits broadly. | Expressly separate warranty, tax, title/fundamental, specific indemnity, debt/price adjustment, fraud and other contractual claims, with tailored caps, thresholds, periods and remedies. | **Define claim categories and their regimes expressly.** A single limitations regime could inadvertently dilute negotiated protections or remedies. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register as evidence of 100% title. | Independent verification of issued capital, ownership, encumbrances and authority to transfer, plus executed transfer documents and title warranties at completion. | **Verify title independently and retain robust title warranties.** The register is the seller-identified source, not proof that the buyer has completed its own checks. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP positions settled under the general regime. | Specific tax and IP warranties, tailored tax covenant/indemnity and IP ownership/non-infringement protections, with appropriate separate caps and survival periods. | **Treat these as open and negotiate them separately.** The seller’s assertion does not supply the missing terms, and general-warranty limits may not fit tax or IP exposure. |

The seller’s “FINAL” and market-practice assertions are negotiating positions, not evidence that the terms were agreed or are acceptable to the buyer. Review these recommendations against the full SPA, diligence record and transaction documents before finalising a mark-up.
=== END ADVICE ===
